items.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002
items.q: you can find Eddie Harris, Ornette Coleman

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah, oh yeah absolutely. Because the foundation of what Billy Higgins is playing on “Freedom Jazz Dance” is right from second line. You can hear it it’s right in there. Ed Blackwell is another one, the rhythms that he played came right out of second line. It was one of the rhythms that fed one of the seeds for swing to develop. Because there’s triplet involved. And it has a way of sort of making the beat and the feel elastic, which gives it

that bounce. So certainly yeah, that’s a part of it. And particularly in “Q-B-Rab,” there’s a lot of elements that I was addressing. And even the record, the whole recording, “Passages,” which is the title of that, the purpose I guess that I had in mind was to bring together all of the influences that I’ve had as a musician and growing up and hearing all of these different kinds of music and jazz and R&B and funk, avante garde, within the thread of that tune you know you can find Eddie Harris, Ornette Coleman,…
